Count recurring paths and meta-paths in the sessions

Source: R/extract_meta_paths.R
extract_meta_paths.Rd

extract_meta_paths() counts the recurring paths and meta-paths in the sessions of an htna network. In a heterogeneous network every code belongs to an actor, so each run of codes in a session has two readings: the concrete path (for example Request->Plan->Execute) and its meta-path, the sequence of actor types it passes through (Human->AI->AI). Meta-paths describe the turn-taking between the actors, such as how often the human intervenes between two AI actions, while the concrete paths say what is done in each turn. Counting both shows which interaction patterns recur and whether they occur more often than the frequencies of their codes would predict.

extract_meta_paths() counts every path of the requested lengths in the sessions of an htna network. With level = "state" (default) it returns concrete paths, each tagged with its meta-path; with level = "type" it returns the meta-paths, summed over their concrete instances. A schema restricts the search to one template whose elements can be actor types (any code of that actor), concrete codes, or "*" (any element), freely mixed: "Human->Ask->*" is any human code, then the AI code Ask, then anything. With type = "gapped", the elements of a path are gap + 1 positions apart instead of adjacent.

It returns a data frame with one row per path and gap. For each path the table gives its count, the number and share (support) of sessions that contain it, its share among the paths of the same length and gap (frequency), and its lift: the count divided by the count expected if the elements occurred independently with their overall frequencies.

To compare paths between groups of sessions use sequence_compare_htna(); for unordered co-occurrence use association_rules_htna().

Usage

extract_meta_paths(
  x,
  level = c("state", "type"),
  length = 2:4,
  schema = NULL,
  type = c("contiguous", "gapped"),
  gap = 1L,
  min_count = 1L,
  min_support = 0,
  min_lift = 0,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  contain = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna().

level

"state" (default) for concrete paths with their meta-path, or "type" for meta-paths only.

length

Path lengths to count (default 2:4); ignored when schema is given.

schema

A template of elements separated by "->"; each element is an actor type, a code or "*". NULL (default) counts all paths.

type

"contiguous" (default) for adjacent elements, or "gapped" for elements gap + 1 positions apart.

gap

Gap or gaps for type = "gapped" (default 1); several values give one set of rows per length and gap.

min_count

Minimum number of occurrences (default 1).

min_support

Minimum share of sessions containing the path (default 0).

min_lift

Minimum lift (default 0, no filter).

start, end, contain

Keep only paths whose first element is in start, whose last element is in end, or that contain every element of contain (default NULL); elements are codes or, with level = "type", actor types.

Value

A data frame of class c("htna_meta_paths", "htna_paths", "data.frame") with one row per path and gap, sorted by length, gap and decreasing count, and columns schema (the path), meta_schema (its meta-path; only with level = "state"), length, gap, count, n_sequences, support, frequency and lift. The number of sessions and the level are kept as attributes and shown by print().

Conditions

Errors of class htna_bad_input for an unknown element in schema or a zero gap with type = "gapped", and htna_unassigned_node when x has no actor partition.

See also

print.htna_paths(), sequence_compare_htna(), association_rules_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
extract_meta_paths(net, level = "type", length = 3)
#> Meta-paths (type-level) over 429 sequences
#> Rows: 8 | Lengths: 3 | Gaps: 0
